probe:cereb-search.summary: P10 reversed the pipeline's search: MRI pieces (body = label 1, cerebellum = label 2, whole tissue = control) were the moving templates and the OCT [WM,GM] class volume (wm_bright=True, the v11 choice; prep reproduced the v11 Otsu thresholds exactly: OCT 19431.7, MRI 1.0211) was searched exhaustively with octreg.search.FFTSearcher at 0.6 mm (8000 rotations x both handedness, topk 24, register.py's adaptive gate). The machinery works: the whole-tissue control lands 3.2 mm (block corners) / 7 deg from P_R5, the body piece 7.8 mm / 18 deg (9.9 mm / 25 deg after the reversed rigid->similarity->affine chain), both proper handedness. The cerebellum piece has NO real match: its best candidate (score 0.251, proper) is a generic, polarity-indifferent fit (with the OCT class polarity flipped it scores HIGHER, 0.261, and mirrored; the body collapses from 0.302 to 0.102 under the same flip), its refined structural NCC is 0.226-0.233 vs 0.298 for the body, its flattened-intensity NCC at 0.3 mm is 0.04-0.05 with no coherent sign (1-2 guard blocks, frac_neg 0.5-1.0; body: 0.148 with 79% negative blocks), MI32 0.08 (body 0.10), and the folia cue is at the random level (0.056-0.059 vs random mean 0.048 / p95 0.075; P_R5 0.040). That best cerebellum pose is not rigidly consistent with the body: it is the body's pose rotated 175 deg about an oblique axis (56/46/62 deg to the body's PCA axes), bbox corners 41 mm / centroid 12 mm apart, and it sits 38% on the deep half of the OCT brainstem body (z 60-125), 53% on the deep folded pieces (z 125-175), 30% on tissue the body itself claims. Placing the MRI cerebellum where the body's pose says it should be (inverse P_R5 / body pose) gives class NCC 0.003-0.107, and register.py's chain from there only reaches 0.110-0.134 while staying consistent (5.6 mm / 10 deg); under the body pose the MRI cerebellum maps to the TOP of the block (z<60: black tiles / agarose, 55% there, 23% outside the array, only 58% on mask). Meanwhile the 0.04 mm close-ups show unmistakable cerebellar folia (rows of rounded lobules with layered cortex and a central WM core; longitudinally cut parallel leaflets with brighter cores) in the deep folded pieces at OCT z 125-175, y 150-240, x 30-120 - torn, with gaps between lobules - i.e. cerebellar tissue IS in the block, at the bottom, on the opposite side of the body from where the MRI (via P_R5) puts it, and no rigid pose of the MRI piece fits it. Verdict: present but not rigidly consistent - the cerebellum pieces moved (detached/folded lobules); the body pose passes its own polarity / handedness / 180-degree tests, and the cerebellum must be excluded from every rigid/affine objective and QC.
probe:cereb-search.recipe: Server work/probe_xr/cereb/p10_cereb.py (stages prep/search/refine/figs), p10_extra.py, p10_extra2.py; GPU (RTX 4090), one job at a time; total ~15 min. PREP: OCT class map = octreg.features.otsu_two_class(oct150, oct150_mask, wm_bright=True) -> [WM=bright, GM]; MRI class map = otsu_two_class_lowmem(mri, mri_tissue, wm_bright=False, vox 0.08) (bias-flattened 10 mm, float16); eroded OCT mask = fine.erode_ball(mask, 1.5 mm) = 9.13 cm3 (from 18.05). SEARCH VOLUME: OCT class map x mask, avg_pool_iso factor 4 -> 0.6 mm (48,66,53), tissue = pooled mask (variants: full mask; eroded mask, features x eroded mask). TEMPLATES: MRI piece (label==k from piece_labels_tex2.npy; whole = mri_tissue) x class map, cropped to the piece bbox (aligned to the pooling factor), avg_pool factor 8 (0.64 mm, as register.py rounds 0.6/0.08). FFTSearcher(oct_feat06, A_oct06, oct_mask06, piece_feat06, A_piece06, piece_mask06, spacing 0.6, min_overlap = min(0.85, max(0.15, 0.8*V_OCTmask/V_template)) = 0.85 for body/cereb/whole with the full mask; 0.78/0.85/0.55 with the eroded mask); own loop over the 16000 orientations (random_rotations(8000, seed 0) + R@diag(1,1,-1)) storing every per-orientation max, then register.py's NMS (3 mm / 10 deg, topk 24) three times: all / proper only / mirrored only (item 4). Where register.py's gate admitted no orientation (whole: 0.85; body eroded 0.78; cereb eroded 0.85) it was relaxed stepwise to 0.70 (reported as gate_used). Extra null: OCT class channels swapped (polarity flip) for cereb, body, whole. Poses: T_m2o = searcher.pose_from (MRI world -> OCT world); T_oct2mri = inv(T_m2o); compared with P_R5 via evaluate.transform_diff + fine.pose_move (block corners of oct150). REFINE (item 3): register.py's polarity-trial chain with the roles swapped - refine.Refiner(oct_feat_L, A_oct_L, piece_feat_L, A_piece_L, piece_mask_L) at 0.6 (rigid, similarity; 120 it), 0.3 (rigid, affine; 200 it), 0.15 (affine; 200 it), ls/sh clamp 0.15, reg 2.0, for cereb top-3 and body top-1 (MRI levels 0.64/0.32/0.16 mm, OCT 0.6/0.3/0.15). Fine measures: fine.Level at 0.3 mm with the PIECE as the MRI tissue (box = piece bbox + 5 mm), m_spec = Level.spec_mask(T) = piece eroded 1.3 mm via T & OCT mask & valid; polarity_guard sign; FineRefiner (sign +1) evaluate_T -> raw NCC, sign-corrected = |NCC| with the guard sign (-1 assumed when mixed); MI32 with edges fixed at the evaluated pose. Folia cue: OCT local std (masked box, window 4 vox = 0.6 mm) > specimen p85 (3021.7) & intensity > specimen median (17038.9) -> 8.6% of the specimen; MRI cerebellum piece eroded 0.5 mm at 0.16 mm (2.50 cm3), 300k points mapped through inv(T_oct2mri), nearest voxel; random reference = 40 poses (random rotation, random handedness, piece centroid on a random specimen voxel). Consistency: Landing.consistency = displacement of the piece's bbox corners / points / centroid between two MRI->OCT poses + rotation angle/axis of the delta (fine.rotation_deg), axis angles to the body's PCA axes; also the cerebellum template scored AT the body's poses (inverse P_R5, body search, body refined) and register.py's chain started there (extra2). Landing description: eroded-piece points -> OCT ijk150, z bands 0-60 / 60-125 (body) / 125-175 (deep folded pieces) / >175, fraction on mask, overlap with the body resampled into OCT at the body's pose and at P_R5. Figures: 3-plane 0.15 mm with the piece resampled (nearest) into OCT space (contour), overview z- and y-slice strips, top-of-block strip (z 6-34), 0.04 mm close-ups from octv.npy (16 mm FOV at the landing centroid) next to the MRI cerebellum at 0.08 mm, and 0.04 mm close-ups at four points inside the deep folded pieces; all downloaded and inspected.

probe:cereb-search.caveats: 1) register.py's overlap gate, swapped (0.8*V_OCTmask/V_template capped at 0.85), admitted no orientation for the whole-tissue control (0.85), the eroded-mask body (0.78) and the eroded-mask cerebellum (0.85); those searches ran at 0.70 (reported as gate_used) - the eroded-mask variants are barely informative (eroded mask 9.13 cm3 vs body 9.35 cm3: only 3 valid orientations, flat landscape) and the eroded-mask cerebellum result (0.199 proper, 169 deg from P_R5, landing centroid (94,113,98), 56% on the body) is the same generic body fit. 2) The piece labels are watershed pieces with tendrils (cerebellum bbox 24x39x28 mm for 4.15 cm3), so the landing bounding boxes span the block; the z-band fractions and centroids (computed on the 0.5 mm-eroded piece, 2.50 cm3) are the meaningful location numbers. 3) Reversed-role refinement uses the piece mask as the point weights (NCC over the piece only), which is the natural swap but not literally register.py's OCT-mask-weighted loss; the fine measures use the piece as the MRI tissue (flattening inside the piece) and MI32 edges fixed at each evaluated pose (fine_stage fixes them at T_fine), so MI values are comparable only loosely across poses. 4) The 'sign-corrected' intensity NCC for the cerebellum uses -1 where the guard is mixed (only 1-2 blocks pass min_vox on a 0.64 cm3 specimen); at P_R5 the cerebellum's m_spec is only 0.24 cm3 (its 0.121 is on a tiny, edge-dominated mask). 5) The body piece alone refines to a pose 25 deg / 9.9 mm (block corners) from P_R5 (points mean 5.1 mm) with better body-piece intensity measures (|NCC| 0.148 / MI 0.102 vs 0.118 / 0.090 at P_R5) - the nearly symmetric body under-constrains rotation and P_R5 was fitted with the whole (agarose-including) OCT mask; the whole-tissue control was not refined (only its search pose, 3.2 mm / 7 deg from P_R5, is reported). This is a side observation outside P10's question. 6) Random-pose folia reference uses 40 poses with the centroid on a specimen voxel (on-mask mean 0.67); the cue itself is 12.5% at z<60 (bright rim / tile edges) so 'high local std & bright' is not a pure folia detector - the decisive folia evidence is visual (fig_deep_pieces_closeup.png). 7) The search scores the body's 180-degree partner at 0.243 vs 0.302 and the body fits poorly at the cerebellum's pose (0.031 / 0.027), which argues against P_R5 being a 180-degree impostor, but P10 did not re-test the body pose beyond that. 8) All GPU/CPU work stayed within work/probe_xr/cereb and /tmp; nothing else was written.
probe:cereb-search.verdict: PRESENT BUT NOT RIGIDLY CONSISTENT - the cerebellum pieces moved. Cerebellar tissue is physically in the OCT block: the deep folded pieces at z 125-175 (y 150-240, x 30-120, bottom of the block) show unmistakable folia at 0.04 mm (lobules with a WM core, layered cortex, parallel leaflets), fragmented with gaps. But the MRI cerebellum piece has no rigid counterpart anywhere: its best exhaustive-search candidate (0.251) is below the polarity-flipped null (0.261, mirrored), i.e. a generic two-class blob fit, with no coherent intensity relation (flattened NCC 0.04-0.05, mixed sign), MI32 0.08, folia cue at the random level (0.056 vs random 0.048 / p95 0.075) even though half of it lies on the folia region, and it is the body's pose rotated 175 deg about an oblique (non-symmetry) axis, sitting on the body's deep half - an impostor fit on the body, not the '180-degree partner' or a mirror partner of the body (same handedness; handedness preference flips only with the class polarity). Placing the MRI cerebellum where the body pose (P_R5 or the body-only pose) says it belongs maps it to the top of the block (z<60: black tiles / agarose; 23% outside the array) and scores 0.00-0.11 even after register.py's chain, while the OCT folia lie at the bottom (z 125-175), on the opposite side of the body. The body pose itself is not contradicted by this probe (whole-tissue control 3.2 mm from P_R5; body's 180-degree partner scores 0.243 vs 0.302; body at the cerebellum's pose 0.031/0.027; body polarity-specific 0.302 vs 0.102). Consequence: the MRI cerebellum (label 2) and the OCT folia at z 125-175 must be excluded from every rigid/affine objective and from QC of the body pose; if the cerebellum is ever to be used it needs its own piecewise / non-rigid registration of the detached lobules, not a shared rigid pose with the body.
